label: Weather
value: Basel 47.56 N 7.59 E, hourly, 2025
source: Open-Meteo historical archive (data/reference_house_2025_hourly.csv), as the case brief asks

label: Days shown
value: Wednesday 15 January 2025 (day 14) and Tuesday 15 July 2025 (day 195)
source: the live app's January and July moments (dashboard/lib/live/shared.ts CONDITIONS); sliced from the full-year run, so the tank carries over. Day index 0 = 1 January, as the live app's "Now"

label: Server
value: 1 kW in, 80% recovered as heat
source: case brief

label: Sites
value: Hospital 38 servers, 70 kWh tank, 60 °C; House 11 servers, 35 kWh tank, 55 °C; Spa & pool 33 servers, 50 kWh tank, 40 °C
source: the live app's base sites (scheduler/balance.py DEFAULT_SITES); tanks and supply temperatures: scheduler/sites.py KINDS defaults (the live app sends no tank size)

label: Building size
value: Hospital x4 the house's coldest hour (42.0 kW); House x1 the house's coldest hour (10.5 kW); Spa & pool x3 the house's coldest hour (31.5 kW)
source: the live app's X_HOUSE (dashboard/lib/live/shared.ts, our assumption): each building's hourly demand is scaled so its coldest hour is X times the house's; it keeps its own daily and yearly shape (scheduler.sites.size_sites, shared with scheduler.day)

label: Servers per site
value: the fewest that, with the site's tank, cover every hour of 2025 (house: 11; the coldest hour alone would need 14)
source: the live app's sizing "tank" (scheduler.sites.tank_servers): the scheduler's own heat permit, hour by hour, with the tank starting the year at its 31 December level; all heat from servers, no heat pump, no backup heater

label: Heat demand
value: House: case formula 10 kW x (20 - T) / 25.6 + 0.5 kW hot water. Hospital: 2,500 kWh hot water per bed and year + ward heating. Spa: pool water, hall at 30 °C, showers and sauna 09-21
source: scheduler/sites.py (hospital DHW study; Passive House pool guide); see docs/assumptions.md

label: Floor area (site card)
value: Hospital 1,910 m²; House 180 m²; Spa & pool 480 m²
source: our assumption: house 180 m²; hospital 40 m² per bed, spa 5 x its water area, both scaled with the building size above (the models size these sites in beds and m² of water, not floor area)

label: Base plan
value: the live app's set-up: tank-sized servers, jobs may move between sites, on/off servers, no dry cooler
source: scheduler.day as the live app calls it; each measure changes one thing

label: Electricity price
value: CHF 0.3325/kWh
source: ElCom 2026, IWB Basel, category H4, total incl. all fees (data/raw/elcom_iwb_H4_2025_2026.json), as the case brief asks

label: Heat pump efficiency (COP)
source: case brief (Swiss field tests measured 2.5-4.0 for air-water, so 2.5 is conservative)

label: Heat-pump heat price
value: CHF 0.1330 per kWh of heat (electricity / 2.5)
source: case brief: value of the heat = electricity price / 2.5

label: DigitalHeat heat price
value: CHF 0.0931/kWh, 30% below a heat pump
source: our assumption, following the case owner (21 Nov 2026): a discount, not free heat (data/business_assumptions.json heat_discount_base, docs/business-model.md section 5)

label: Host pays half the power
value: 50% of the server electricity (incl. dry cooler fan), no heat price
source: DigitalHeat meeting, 21 Nov 2026: "host pays at least 50 % of power". docs/business-model.md section 5: for a home this costs more than a heat pump

label: Computing sell price
value: CHF 3.423/server-hour
source: AWS spot for the same server (c7a.48xlarge, Frankfurt) USD 3.26 x USD/CHF 0.84 = CHF 2.738 (data/prices_2026.json, checked Nov 2026), plus 25% for local, private, Swiss computing (data/business_assumptions.json compute_premium, our assumption; case owner: we can charge more than Amazon). The live app quotes the same. On-demand would be CHF 9.445

label: Server-hours sold
value: every server-hour that runs is sold
source: scheduler/balance.py (as in the case's key figures); docs/business-model.md's investor view assumes 70 % sold

label: Hardware
value: CHF 25,000 per server, written off over 5 years
source: data/prices_2026.json (listed dual EPYC 9654 server + about 30 % for 2026 memory and cooling)

label: DigitalHeat profit
value: income - electricity DigitalHeat pays + what the host pays for heat - hardware
source: ours; scheduler/balance.py credits the full heat value instead of the discounted heat price (difference: 30% of the heat value)

label: Break-even price
value: (electricity - heat value) / server-hours sold
source: case brief, as scheduler/balance.py

label: Dry cooler fan
value: 0.02 kW per kW of heat rejected
source: Kelvion datasheet, design point (scheduler/core.py)

label: CO₂ of Swiss electricity
value: 90 g CO₂eq/kWh
source: VSE (Swiss electricity industry association), 2026: Swiss consumption mix 2025, incl. imports, direct and upstream emissions (strom.ch)

label: CO₂ of the data centre's electricity
value: 344 g CO₂/kWh
source: Umweltbundesamt (German Environment Agency), 2026: German consumption mix 2025, preliminary. Direct CO₂ only, so the data-centre side is if anything understated

label: Data centre
value: AWS Frankfurt (eu-central-1), PUE 1.14
source: the comparator instance of data/prices_2026.json; PUE: AWS sustainability page, global PUE 2025 (aws.amazon.com/sustainability). Location-based factor, no green-power certificates; its heat is wasted

label: CO₂ without DigitalHeat
value: heat demand / COP x Swiss factor + the same server-hours x 1 kW x PUE x German factor
source: ours

label: CO₂ with DigitalHeat
value: top-up heat / COP x Swiss factor + server electricity incl. fan x Swiss factor
source: ours

label: Always-on comparison
value: every server runs every hour, 0.8 kW of heat each into the tank, heat above the tank is dumped; tank empty on 1 January; same prices
source: ours (no scheduler)

label: Always-on comparison: cooler not charged
value: the always-on servers dump heat the tank cannot take, which needs a dry cooler or the servers overheat; its cost (about CHF 550 per kW installed) and fan power are not charged, so the always-on income and CO₂ figures are flattering
source: ours; dry cooler cost: data/business_assumptions.json drycooler_chf_per_kw

label: Strategy rules
value: a plan qualifies only if every host pays at most what its own heat pump would cost and the plan pays off. Best value = profit - capex / 5 years (no interest). Safest = no capex, no heat dumped, no job missed, then most profit. Ties: fewer measures
source: ours; the plans are searched by scripts/build_sim2.py, not hand-picked

label: CO₂ if the data centre ran on Swiss power
value: base plan saves 19.3 t a year instead of 154.5 t
source: ours, sensitivity: most of the saving comes from the cleaner Swiss grid; the heat reuse and the data centre's cooling overhead (PUE) are the rest
